facts: GitLabContentSchema includes optional last_commit_id on repository-file read results.
CreateOrUpdateFileSchema exposes project_id, file_path, content, commit_message, branch, and optional previous_path, but no last_commit_id.
It passes project_id, file_path, content, commit_message, branch, and previous_path to createOrUpdateFile; no last_commit_id argument exists on the screened path.
createOrUpdateFile invokes getFileContents only to determine whether to use POST or PUT and discards the returned GitLabContent object.
For an existing file, the request body contains branch, content, commit_message, and optional previous_path.
The effectful PUT body contains no last_commit_id.

authoritative_source_evidence.authority: GitLab official Repository Files API documentation
facts: Repository-file retrieval returns last_commit_id, the SHA of the last commit that modified the file.
Update file accepts optional last_commit_id, described as the last known file commit ID.
A successful update returns 200 OK; failed commits return 400 Bad Request with a non-specific error.
For an existing-file PUT with last_commit_id set to the prior commit for the path, the spec requires HTTP 400 and the message that the file changed since editing began.
For the same update profile with last_commit_id equal to the current last commit for the path, the spec requires HTTP 200 OK.

open_evidence_limits: Current GitLab API documentation is retrieval-time web evidence; the exact stale/correct guard behavior is additionally anchored by an immutable official upstream request-spec revision.
The target claim is a static realization claim at the pinned MCP revision; no live GitLab deployment conformance is claimed.
No claim is made about other MCP tools or direct GitLab API callers that can supply last_commit_id.
